name: Pegfilgrastim
route_note: single SC injection once per chemotherapy cycle, at least 24 hours after chemotherapy; on-body injector available
owner: Amgen (Neulasta); biosimilars (Viatris/Biocon, Coherus, Sandoz and others)

discovery.note: A 20 kDa polyethylene glycol chain is attached to the N-terminal methionine of filgrastim, reducing renal clearance.

tagline: Pegylated G-CSF given once per chemotherapy cycle
summary: Pegfilgrastim is filgrastim covalently linked to a 20 kDa polyethylene glycol, which reduces renal clearance so a single dose per chemotherapy cycle replaces daily injections. It lowers the incidence of febrile neutropenia in patients receiving myelosuppressive chemotherapy. Several biosimilars are available.
mechanism: Like filgrastim, pegfilgrastim activates the G-CSF receptor on neutrophil precursors, increasing neutrophil production and release from the marrow.

PEGylation makes the molecule too large for glomerular filtration, so clearance depends mainly on binding to neutrophils. Levels therefore stay high during the neutropenic nadir and fall as neutrophil counts recover, a self-regulating clearance.
uses: Reduction of febrile neutropenia with myelosuppressive chemotherapy for non-myeloid malignancies
Haematopoietic syndrome of acute radiation syndrome

history.title: Parent drug
history.detail: Filgrastim (Neupogen) approved; daily dosing motivates a long-acting form.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Neulasta approved for once-per-cycle dosing; EU approval follows in 2002.

history.title: On-body injector
history.detail: Neulasta Onpro kit allows automatic delivery about 27 hours after application.

history.title: Radiation syndrome
history.detail: Approved for haematopoietic subsyndrome of acute radiation syndrome.

history.title: US biosimilars
history.detail: Fulphila (Mylan/Biocon) and Udenyca (Coherus) become the first US pegfilgrastim biosimilars.

pk.half_life: about 15–80 hours, depending on neutrophil count

facts: Fulphila (pegfilgrastim-jmdb), approved by the FDA in June 2018, was the first pegfilgrastim biosimilar in the US.
The Neulasta Onpro on-body injector is applied on the day of chemotherapy and delivers the dose about 27 hours later.
